title: 2005 HMMT February General Round 2 Problem 3
statement: Working together, Jack and Jill can paint a house in 3 days; Jill and Joe can paint the same house in 4 days; or Joe and Jack can paint the house in 6 days. If Jill, Joe, and Jack all work together, how many days will it take them?

solutions.text:
\(8 / 3\)
Suppose that Jack paints \(x\) houses per day, Jill paints \(y\) houses per day, and Joe paints \(z\) houses per day. Together, Jack and Jill paint \(1 / 3\) of a house in a day - that is,

\[x+y=1 / 3 .\]

Similarly,

\[y+z=1 / 4\]

and

\[z+x=1 / 6\]

Adding all three equations and dividing by 2 gives

\[x+y+z=3 / 8\]

So, working together, the three folks can paint \(3 / 8\) houses in a day, or \(8 / 3\) days per house.
